question: What is the primary purpose of a health insurance scheme?

options.A: To generate profits for pharmaceutical companies
options.B: To protect people from high out-of-pocket medical costs
options.C: To provide free salaries for healthcare workers
options.D: To eliminate all diseases in the community

explanation: Insurance pools financial resources so that sudden medical emergencies do not cause total financial ruin for individuals. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h1)

question: Risk pooling works effectively because:

options.A: Contributions from many healthy people cover the care costs of the few who fall sick
options.B: The government pays all hospital bills instantly
options.C: Only sick people contribute money to the fund
options.D: Healthy people pay for their care without any help

explanation: The financial risk is shared among a large group where the healthy subsidize the sick. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h1)

question: The national body regulating health insurance in Nigeria is the:
explanation: The NHIA oversees the implementation and regulation of health insurance across the country. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h2)

question: Formal sector employees enrolled in national schemes usually pay their premiums through:

options.A: Contributions shared between the employer and employee
options.B: Daily cash payments at the hospital pharmacy

explanation: Formal sector arrangements often involve a joint contribution split between the worker and the organization. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h2)

question: State Health Insurance Agencies are primarily designed to cater to:

options.A: Federal ministers and top politicians exclusively
options.B: Patients admitted to private specialist clinics abroad
options.C: Only foreign nationals living in cities
options.D: Residents within a specific state, including informal workers

explanation: State schemes bridge the gap by extending coverage to people outside the federal civil service. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h3)

question: Community-based health insurance is most successful because it relies on:

options.B: Mandatory deductions from international oil companies
options.D: Local trust and active participation of community members

explanation: Grassroots ownership ensures that members understand and willingly contribute to their local health fund. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h3)

question: Private health insurance plans are typically funded by:

options.B: Free grants from the World Health Organization
options.C: Automatic deductions from public secondary school teachers
options.D: Voluntary purchase by individuals or corporate employers

explanation: People or businesses buy private plans voluntarily to secure additional healthcare benefits. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h4)

question: A major characteristic of private health insurance compared to basic public schemes is:

options.A: It often offers access to luxury private facilities for higher premiums
options.B: It is completely free for all citizens
options.C: It is strictly managed by village elders

explanation: Private providers use tiered pricing structures to offer premium hospital environments and specialized care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h4)

question: The process of combining financial contributions from many people to pay for medical care is called:
explanation: Risk pooling spreads the financial burden of illness across a large, diverse group of contributors. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h5)

question: Why is adverse selection a threat to health insurance schemes?

options.A: Only healthy people refuse to register for insurance
options.B: The government stops collecting taxes from civil servants
options.C: Hospitals refuse to treat patients who have insurance cards
options.D: Only people who expect high medical bills tend to buy coverage, draining the fund

explanation: When only the sick enroll, the pool lacks enough healthy contributions to sustain payouts. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h5)

question: A key administrative duty of a nurse regarding health insurance is to:

options.A: Verify the patient's insurance status and document care
options.C: Collect taxes for the federal government
options.D: Determine the annual premium rates for the insurance company

explanation: Nurses check eligibility and record clinical services to facilitate smooth reimbursement from the scheme. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h6)

question: Patient education by nurses regarding health insurance helps to:

options.A: Force patients to pay cash for free services
options.B: Prevent misunderstandings about covered services and reduce delays
options.C: Stop patients from visiting the hospital entirely

explanation: Educating clients on their benefits ensures they know what is covered and prevents friction during billing. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h6)
